titre: The Chrysler Building's Spire Was Raised in Secret in 90 Minutes
accroche: In October 1929, a 56-meter steel needle rose from the top of the Chrysler Building, assembled in secret inside the frame.
contenu_vulgarise:
By the spring of 1929, two New York building sites are secretly racing for the title of tallest building in the world. At 40 Wall Street, developer George Ohrstrom is building a tower designed by H. Craig Severance: by April, it reaches 282 meters (927 feet), enough to surpass every tower under construction. A few blocks away, William Van Alen is raising a tower crowned with stainless-steel scales for industrialist Walter Chrysler. Van Alen and Severance know each other well: they used to be partners.

## A Spire Raised in Under Two Hours

Van Alen has permission to add a spire, but he reveals its real height to no one. It's assembled in secret, in four sections, inside the Chrysler Building's own frame, out of sight of onlookers and of the rival site. On October 23, 1929, the first section, anchored to the top of the dome, is lowered and fixed to the 66th floor; the other three sections follow, hoisted and riveted in about ninety minutes. The steel needle reaches 56 meters (185 feet), on a base 2.4 meters (8 feet) square, and weighs 27 tons. Van Alen, the engineers, and Walter Chrysler watch the operation from the street. Spire included, the Chrysler Building reaches 319 meters (1,046 feet), surpassing 40 Wall Street outright. The press stays quiet at first: the New York Herald Tribune, which had been following the site closely, doesn't report the spire's raising until several days later.

## A Record That Lasts Only a Year

The Chrysler Building officially becomes the tallest building in the world on May 27, 1930. But the developer of the Empire State Building, John J. Raskob, had already announced his own project before the Chrysler was even finished. Raskob has his tower extended by five floors and a spire, reaching 320 meters (1,050 feet) at the observatory. On May 1, 1931, a little less than a year after the Chrysler, the Empire State Building takes the title away.

## What This Spire Shifts

The Chrysler Building remains one of New York's most photographed skyscrapers today, for a crown it held, as a world record, for only eleven months. Its spire doesn't owe its fame to how long it stayed at the top of the ranking, but to the way it got there: a gesture by an architect designed less to last than to catch a rival off guard on the one day no reply was still possible. Van Alen himself never claimed this feat as a personal act of revenge against his former partner; history has remembered it that way regardless.

repere.texte: The Chrysler Building's spire, 56 meters (185 feet) tall and 2.4 meters wide at its base, weighs 27 tons. Its four sections were hoisted and riveted into place in about ninety minutes, on October 23, 1929, bringing the tower to 319 meters (1,046 feet).

carte.punch: The Chrysler Building's spire was raised in secret, in 90 minutes, to beat a rival.
carte.idee: In 1929, William Van Alen has a 56-meter spire secretly assembled inside the Chrysler Building's frame. Hoisted and riveted in 90 minutes on October 23, it brings the tower to 319 meters, instantly overtaking its rival at 40 Wall Street.

quiz.question: Why was the real height of the Chrysler Building's spire kept secret until it was raised?
choix: To comply with a confidentiality clause imposed by the City of New York
Because the final plans hadn't yet been settled
To create a surprise at the building's official opening
To stop the rival site at 40 Wall Street from raising its own tower in response
quiz.explication: Van Alen had watched his former partner Severance raise 40 Wall Street every time a new height was announced. By assembling the spire in secret inside the frame, he prevented any reply before the Chrysler Building was finished.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What final height, including the spire, does the Chrysler Building reach in 1930?
quiz_supplementaire.explication: 282 meters (927 feet) is the height targeted for 40 Wall Street, and 320 meters (1,050 feet) is that of the Empire State Building's observatory. The Chrysler Building, spire included, reaches 319 meters (1,046 feet).

quiz_supplementaire.question: How long does the Chrysler Building remain the tallest building in the world?
choix: Ten years, until World War II
A little less than a year, until the Empire State Building opens in 1931
Only a few weeks, before 40 Wall Street was completed
It never held the title, which went straight to 40 Wall Street
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The Chrysler Building becomes the tallest building in the world on May 27, 1930, and loses the title on May 1, 1931, to the Empire State Building: a little less than a year.
